#!/usr/bin/env bash
# [#1801/SPEC-1] A run hook that hangs is killed at the per-stage timeout on
# every dispatch route — map, fanout, sequential strategy, roleless leaf, cycle
# member, parallel-group member, and always_run — and the stage ends with
# disposition timed_out naming the stage and the limit.
#
# [#1801/SPEC-10] _runner_dispatch_always_run and _orch_local_collect_results
# kill through zbuild_pg_kill; no hand-rolled TERM/KILL sequence remains for
# stage dispatch.
#
# [#1801/SPEC-17] The per-dispatch timeout watchdog kills a hung hook under
# the orch-mock backend (confirming the watchdog in lifecycle.sh is
# backend-agnostic); plugins/tool/orch-ruflo-hive/plugin.sh carries no
# TERM/KILL sequence that would suppress the lifecycle-level kill.
#
# All dispatch routes reach plugin_hook_call in lifecycle.sh; the single
# watchdog there covers every route. These tests FAIL on pre-change code
# (where lifecycle.sh has no watchdog) and PASS after the change.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "[#1801/SPEC-1/SPEC-10/SPEC-17] per-dispatch stage timeout watchdog"
setup_test_env "stage-timeout-dispatch"

_lc="$REPO_ROOT/core/plugin-registry/lifecycle.sh"

# ─── Extract plugin_hook_call body for inspection ────────────────────────────
_phc_body=""
if [[ -f "$_lc" ]]; then
    _phc_body="$(awk '/^plugin_hook_call\(\) \{/{p=1} p{print} p && /^\}$/{exit}' "$_lc" 2>/dev/null || true)"
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-1] lifecycle.sh has a per-dispatch timeout watchdog ──────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-1] plugin_hook_call has a timeout watchdog for the run hook"

if [[ -z "$_phc_body" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] plugin_hook_call is defined in lifecycle.sh" "not found"
else
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] plugin_hook_call is defined in lifecycle.sh"

    # The watchdog must be armed only for the `run` hook (not cleanup/other hooks).
    # Check for a guard like `[[ "$hook_name" == "run" ]]` near the timeout code.
    if grep -qE '"run"' <<< "$_phc_body" && grep -q 'zbuild_pg_kill\|zbuild_pid_kill' <<< "$_phc_body"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] watchdog in plugin_hook_call is guarded to run hook only"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] watchdog in plugin_hook_call is guarded to run hook only" \
            "zbuild_pg_kill/zbuild_pid_kill not found inside plugin_hook_call — no per-dispatch watchdog"
    fi
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-1] the watchdog writes timed_out disposition ─────────────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-1] watchdog writes disposition timed_out"

# The watchdog must call the disposition layer with 'timed_out' when it fires.
# Check lifecycle.sh and disposition-writing helpers used from within lifecycle.sh.
_timed_out_found=0
if grep -q 'timed_out' "$_lc" 2>/dev/null; then
    _timed_out_found=1
fi
# Also check that the runner or a helper wires the watchdog result to timed_out
_runner="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"
if grep -q 'timed_out' "$_runner" 2>/dev/null; then
    _timed_out_found=1
fi

if [[ "$_timed_out_found" -eq 1 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] timed_out disposition is used in the dispatch path"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] timed_out disposition is used in the dispatch path" \
        "'timed_out' not found in lifecycle.sh or runner.sh — timeout result cannot produce the required disposition"
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-1] every dispatch route reaches plugin_hook_call ─────────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-1] all dispatch routes lead through plugin_hook_call"

# The design states: all dispatch routes — map, fanout, sequential strategy,
# roleless leaf, cycle member, parallel-group member, always_run — reach
# plugin_hook_call. Verify that each strategy file and the runner itself calls
# plugin_hook_call (not a private bypass).
for _sf in \
    core/pipeline/strategies/fanout.sh \
    core/pipeline/strategies/sequential.sh \
    core/pipeline/strategies/map.sh \
    core/pipeline/runner.sh; do
    _file="$REPO_ROOT/$_sf"
    [[ -f "$_file" ]] || continue
    if grep -q 'plugin_hook_call' "$_file"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] $_sf reaches plugin_hook_call (route covered by watchdog)"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] $_sf reaches plugin_hook_call (route covered by watchdog)" \
            "plugin_hook_call not found — this dispatch route would bypass the watchdog"
    fi
done

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-10] no hand-rolled TERM/KILL in lifecycle.sh for dispatch ────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-10] lifecycle.sh has no hand-rolled TERM/KILL for stage dispatch"

if [[ -n "$_phc_body" ]]; then
    # After the change: no `kill -TERM` or `kill -KILL` hand-rolled in
    # plugin_hook_call itself — these are replaced by zbuild_pg_kill.
    # Allow lines that are purely comments.
    _hand_rolled=""
    _hand_rolled="$(grep -E 'kill -TERM|kill -KILL' <<< "$_phc_body" | grep -v '^\s*#' || true)"
    if [[ -n "$_hand_rolled" ]]; then
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] plugin_hook_call has no hand-rolled TERM/KILL for stage dispatch" \
            "found: $(printf '%s' "$_hand_rolled" | head -3 | tr '\n' '|') — replace with zbuild_pg_kill"
    else
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-10] plugin_hook_call has no hand-rolled TERM/KILL for stage dispatch"
    fi
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-10] _orch_local_collect_results uses zbuild_pg_kill ──────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-10] _orch_local_collect_results uses zbuild_pg_kill"

_le="$REPO_ROOT/core/orch/local_engine.sh"
if [[ ! -f "$_le" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] core/orch/local_engine.sh exists" "not found"
else
    if grep -q 'zbuild_pg_kill\|zbuild_pid_kill' "$_le"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-10] local_engine.sh uses zbuild_pg_kill/zbuild_pid_kill"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] local_engine.sh uses zbuild_pg_kill/zbuild_pid_kill" \
            "not found — _orch_local_collect_results still has a hand-rolled kill sequence"
    fi

    # The old _orch_local_kill_slot is replaced; if it still exists, that is a bug.
    if grep -q '_orch_local_kill_slot' "$_le"; then
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] _orch_local_kill_slot is removed from local_engine.sh" \
            "still present — the hand-rolled kill helper was not replaced by zbuild_pg_kill"
    else
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-10] _orch_local_kill_slot is removed from local_engine.sh"
    fi
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-17] watchdog is backend-agnostic: lifecycle is above backends ─
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-17] watchdog in lifecycle.sh is backend-agnostic (above the backend layer)"

# The watchdog's position in lifecycle.sh (plugin_hook_call) means it fires
# regardless of which orch backend is active — the backends dispatch work units
# that ultimately call plugin_hook_call. Verify orch-mock still routes through it.
_mock_plugin="$REPO_ROOT/plugins/tool/orch-mock/plugin.sh"
if [[ ! -f "$_mock_plugin" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-17] plugins/tool/orch-mock/plugin.sh exists" "not found"
else
    # orch-mock dispatches work units that call plugin_hook_call;
    # the backend itself does not arm or disarm the watchdog.
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-17] orch-mock plugin exists (backend-agnostic watchdog can be tested with it)"
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-17] ruflo-hive carries no suppressing TERM/KILL sequence ─────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-17] orch-ruflo-hive/plugin.sh has no TERM/KILL for stage dispatch"

_hive="$REPO_ROOT/plugins/tool/orch-ruflo-hive/plugin.sh"
if [[ ! -f "$_hive" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-17] plugins/tool/orch-ruflo-hive/plugin.sh exists" "not found"
else
    # The hive plugin must not have a kill -TERM / kill -KILL that would intercept
    # the lifecycle-level watchdog's signal before it reaches the hook subshell.
    # (Pool-management kills in the backend's own shutdown are acceptable.)
    _hive_kills=""
    _hive_kills="$(grep -n 'kill -TERM\|kill -KILL' "$_hive" | grep -v '^\s*#' || true)"
    if [[ -n "$_hive_kills" ]]; then
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-17] orch-ruflo-hive/plugin.sh carries no TERM/KILL for stage dispatch" \
            "found kill -TERM/-KILL in ruflo-hive — may suppress lifecycle-level watchdog signal:" \
            "$(printf '%s' "$_hive_kills" | head -5 | tr '\n' '|')"
    else
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-17] orch-ruflo-hive/plugin.sh carries no TERM/KILL for stage dispatch"
    fi
fi

cleanup_test_env
print_test_results
exit $((FAIL > 0))

3	# child ignoring TERM leaves no process alive after TERM + 10 s grace.

13	# These tests use source-level checks — the behavioral guarantee (no process
14	# survives) is enforced by SPEC-6b in the integration test. These FAIL on

23	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh

33	_phc_body=""
34	if [[ -f "$_lc" ]]; then
35	    _phc_body="$(awk '/^plugin_hook_call\(\) \{/{p=1} p{print} p && /^\}$/{exit}' "$_lc" 2>/dev/null || true)"
36	fi
37	
38	if [[ -z "$_phc_body" ]]; then
39	    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] plugin_hook_call is defined in lifecycle.sh" "not found"
40	else
41	    # set -m inside the function creates a new process group for the backgrounded subshell

43	        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-2] plugin_hook_call uses set -m to give the hook its own process group"

55	        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-2] plugin_hook_call uses zbuild_pg_kill (sends signal to whole group)"
56	    else
57	        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] plugin_hook_call uses zbuild_pg_kill (sends signal to whole group)" \
58	            "zbuild_pg_kill not found — a single-PID kill cannot reach descendants that ignore TERM"
59	    fi
60	fi

63	print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-2] zbuild_pg_kill uses TERM then KILL after grace (proc-group.sh)"
64

66	if [[ ! -f "$_pg" ]]; then
67	    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] scripts/lib/proc-group.sh exists" "not found"
68	else
69	    # zbuild_pg_kill must delegate to _zbuild_pg_term_then_kill, which does

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# [#1801/SPEC-2] Killing a hung run hook stops the entire process group — a
# child ignoring TERM leaves no process alive after TERM + 10 s grace.
#
# The per-dispatch watchdog must:
#   1. Run the hook subshell under set -m (job-control mode) so the subshell
#      becomes a process-group leader.
#   2. Kill via zbuild_pg_kill, which sends TERM to the whole group and then
#      KILL after a grace period.
#   3. The grace period must be at least 10 s (so a hook that traps TERM has
#      enough time to flush, but a child ignoring TERM is killed).
#
# These tests use source-level checks — the behavioral guarantee (no process
# survives) is enforced by SPEC-6b in the integration test. These FAIL on
# pre-change code (where lifecycle.sh has no watchdog at all) and PASS after.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "[#1801/SPEC-2] hung run hook kills entire process group (TERM + 10 s grace + KILL)"

_lc="$REPO_ROOT/core/plugin-registry/lifecycle.sh"

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-2] plugin_hook_call arms the hook under set -m ──────────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-2] plugin_hook_call runs the hook under set -m (creates a process group)"

_phc_body=""
if [[ -f "$_lc" ]]; then
    _phc_body="$(awk '/^plugin_hook_call\(\) \{/{p=1} p{print} p && /^\}$/{exit}' "$_lc" 2>/dev/null || true)"
fi

if [[ -z "$_phc_body" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] plugin_hook_call is defined in lifecycle.sh" "not found"
else
    # set -m inside the function creates a new process group for the backgrounded subshell
    if grep -q 'set -m' <<< "$_phc_body"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-2] plugin_hook_call uses set -m to give the hook its own process group"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] plugin_hook_call uses set -m to give the hook its own process group" \
            "'set -m' not found in plugin_hook_call — the hook's group cannot be signalled"
    fi
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-2] the kill goes through zbuild_pg_kill (group-scope) ────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-2] the timeout kill uses zbuild_pg_kill (group scope, not single-PID)"

if [[ -n "$_phc_body" ]]; then
    if grep -q 'zbuild_pg_kill' <<< "$_phc_body"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-2] plugin_hook_call uses zbuild_pg_kill (sends signal to whole group)"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] plugin_hook_call uses zbuild_pg_kill (sends signal to whole group)" \
            "zbuild_pg_kill not found — a single-PID kill cannot reach descendants that ignore TERM"
    fi
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-2] zbuild_pg_kill uses TERM + grace + KILL ──────────────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-2] zbuild_pg_kill uses TERM then KILL after grace (proc-group.sh)"

_pg="$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/proc-group.sh"
if [[ ! -f "$_pg" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] scripts/lib/proc-group.sh exists" "not found"
else
    # zbuild_pg_kill must delegate to _zbuild_pg_term_then_kill, which does
    # TERM → poll → KILL.
    if grep -q '_zbuild_pg_term_then_kill' "$_pg"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-2] zbuild_pg_kill uses TERM+grace+KILL sequence (_zbuild_pg_term_then_kill)"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] zbuild_pg_kill uses TERM+grace+KILL sequence (_zbuild_pg_term_then_kill)" \
            "_zbuild_pg_term_then_kill not found in proc-group.sh"
    fi
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-2] the grace is at least 10 s ───────────────────────────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-2] the watchdog grace period is at least 10 s"

# The design specifies TERM + 10 s grace + KILL. Verify that the watchdog in
# lifecycle.sh passes a grace of >= 10 to zbuild_pg_kill or that the default
# grace in _zbuild_pg_grace is sufficiently large.
# Check that the value 10 (or larger) appears in the context of zbuild_pg_kill
# invocations in lifecycle.sh.
if [[ -n "$_phc_body" ]]; then
    # Look for zbuild_pg_kill called with a numeric grace >= 10.
    # Accept the pattern: zbuild_pg_kill "$var" 10 or zbuild_pg_kill "$pid" "$grace"
    # where the literal in the source is >= 10.
    _grace_ok=0
    if grep -qE 'zbuild_pg_kill.*[[:space:]][0-9]+' <<< "$_phc_body"; then
        # Extract all numeric values following zbuild_pg_kill
        while IFS= read -r _val; do
            [[ "$_val" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "$_val" -ge 10 ]] && { _grace_ok=1; break; }
        done < <(grep -oE 'zbuild_pg_kill[^)]*' <<< "$_phc_body" | grep -oE '[0-9]+' || true)
    fi
    # Also accept if the grace is passed via a variable (the design uses a configurable grace)
    if grep -qE 'zbuild_pg_kill[^)]*\$\{?[A-Za-z_]' <<< "$_phc_body"; then
        _grace_ok=1
    fi

    if [[ "$_grace_ok" -eq 1 ]]; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-2] watchdog grace period is >= 10 s (or variable-derived)"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] watchdog grace period is >= 10 s (or variable-derived)" \
            "no zbuild_pg_kill call with grace >= 10 found in plugin_hook_call"
    fi
fi

print_test_results
exit $((FAIL > 0))

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# [#1801/SPEC-4] The template loader rejects a stage_timeout_s value below
# the stage's router.timeout_s, and rejects a non-integer value.

print_test_header "[#1801/SPEC-4] template loader validates stage_timeout_s"
setup_test_env "stage-timeout-loader-validation"

_MINIMAL_HEAD='id: t
name: T
extends: null
defaults:
  strategy: fanout
'

_write_tpl() {
    printf '%s%s' "$_MINIMAL_HEAD" "$2" > "$1"
}

# ─── Reject: stage_timeout_s < router.timeout_s ───────────────────────────────

_tpl_low="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/low.yaml"

  - alpha

alpha:
  gate: auto
  roles: [intake]
  stage_timeout_s: 30
  router:
    timeout_s: 600
  io:
    destinations: [file]
'

_rc_low=0
load_template "$_tpl_low" >/dev/null 2>&1 || _rc_low=$?
assert_exit_code "[#1801/SPEC-4] stage_timeout_s=30 below router.timeout_s=600 is rejected (rc=1)" \

  - beta

beta:
  gate: auto
  roles: [intake]
  stage_timeout_s: "1h"
  io:
    destinations: [file]
'

print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-4] stage_timeout_s at or above router.timeout_s is accepted"

_tpl_ok="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/ok.yaml"

gamma:

  roles: [intake]
  stage_timeout_s: 1200

  io:
    destinations: [file]

load_template "$_tpl_ok" >/dev/null 2>&1 || _rc_ok=$?
assert_exit_code "[#1801/SPEC-4] stage_timeout_s=1200 >= router.timeout_s=600 is accepted (rc=0)" \
    "0" "$_rc_ok"
assert_eq "[#1801/SPEC-4] accepted template exports _TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_gamma=1200" \
    "1200" "${_TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_gamma:-<unset>}"

delta:

  roles: [intake]
  stage_timeout_s: 900
  io:
    destinations: [file]
'
_rc_nr=0
load_template "$_tpl_norouter" >/dev/null 2>&1 || _rc_nr=$?
assert_exit_code "[#1801/SPEC-4] stage_timeout_s with no router block is accepted (rc=0)" \
    "0" "$_rc_nr"
assert_eq "[#1801/SPEC-4] exports _TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_delta=900" \
    "900" "${_TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_delta:-<unset>}"

# ─── Accept: equal values (stage_timeout_s == router.timeout_s) ───────────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-4] stage_timeout_s equal to router.timeout_s is accepted"

_tpl_eq="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/eq.yaml"

    destinations: [file]

    "0" "$_rc_eq"

cleanup_test_env
print_test_results
exit $((FAIL > 0))

# that was started before the first attempt would expire during a later retry,

# armed inside the per-dispatch code path (lifecycle.sh / plugin_hook_call),
# not in a shared wrapper above it. They FAIL on pre-change code (where no

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh

print_test_header "[#1801/SPEC-5] retried stage and each map member get a fresh independent timer"

# ─── The watchdog lives inside plugin_hook_call, not in a caller ──────────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-5] timeout watchdog is inside plugin_hook_call (fresh per dispatch)"

_lc="$REPO_ROOT/core/plugin-registry/lifecycle.sh"
if [[ ! -f "$_lc" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-5] lifecycle.sh exists" "not found: $_lc"
else
    # Extract plugin_hook_call's body.
    _phc_body=""
    _phc_body="$(awk '/^plugin_hook_call\(\) \{/{p=1} p{print} p && /^\}$/{exit}' "$_lc" 2>/dev/null || true)"

    if [[ -z "$_phc_body" ]]; then
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-5] plugin_hook_call is defined in lifecycle.sh" \
            "function body not found"
    else
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-5] plugin_hook_call is defined in lifecycle.sh"

        # The watchdog must be inside the function — a timer started here is
        # fresh for every call, whether that call is a retry or a map member.
        if grep -q 'zbuild_pg_kill\|zbuild_pid_kill' <<< "$_phc_body"; then
            assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-5] watchdog (zbuild_pg_kill/zbuild_pid_kill) is inside plugin_hook_call → fresh per dispatch"
        else

    fi

print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-5] runner.sh retry loop dispatches through plugin_hook_call"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# [#1801/SPEC-6] _runner_dispatch_always_run reads stage_timeout_s (not
# router.timeout_s) for its time limit; simple.yaml carries stage_timeout_s
# for all stages at required values; router.timeout_s remains absent from the
# two always_run stages.
#
# [#1801/SPEC-10] _runner_dispatch_always_run kills through zbuild_pg_kill;
# no hand-rolled TERM/KILL sequence remains for stage dispatch.
#
# These tests FAIL on pre-change code (where _runner_dispatch_always_run reads
# _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_* and uses a hand-rolled kill sequence) and PASS
# after the change.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "[#1801/SPEC-6] always_run uses stage_timeout_s; [#1801/SPEC-10] zbuild_pg_kill"
setup_test_env "stage-timeout-always-run"

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-6] runner.sh reads _TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_*, not _ROUTER_TIMEOUT ─
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-6] _runner_dispatch_always_run reads _TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_*"

_runner="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"

# Extract the _runner_dispatch_always_run function body.
_ar_body=""
_ar_body="$(awk '/_runner_dispatch_always_run\(\) \{/{p=1} p{print} p && /^    \}$/{exit}' "$_runner" 2>/dev/null || true)"

if [[ -z "$_ar_body" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-6] _runner_dispatch_always_run is defined in runner.sh" \
        "function body not found"
else
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-6] _runner_dispatch_always_run is defined in runner.sh"

    # After the change: reads _TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_*, not _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_*
    if grep -q '_TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_' <<< "$_ar_body"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-6] _runner_dispatch_always_run reads _TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_*"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-6] _runner_dispatch_always_run reads _TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_*" \
            "_TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_* not found — still using old _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_* or ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT"
    fi

    # The OLD variable must not be the primary source.
    # It may still exist as a fallback to ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S, but
    # _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_* must NOT be the limit variable the function uses.
    if grep -q '_ar_to.*_TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT\|_TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT.*_ar_to' <<< "$_ar_body"; then
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-6] _runner_dispatch_always_run no longer uses _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_* as its time limit" \
            "still reads _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_* for _ar_to — must use _TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_* instead"
    else
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-6] _runner_dispatch_always_run no longer uses _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_* as its time limit"
    fi
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-6] simple.yaml carries stage_timeout_s for all stages ────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-6] simple.yaml stage_timeout_s values"

_simple="$REPO_ROOT/config/templates/simple.yaml"
if [[ ! -f "$_simple" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-6] config/templates/simple.yaml exists" "not found"
else
    # Verify required stage_timeout_s values by parsing the template.
    # Each check verifies that the section contains `stage_timeout_s: N`.
    # Strategy: for each stage, confirm that stage_timeout_s appears in simple.yaml
    # with the required value by extracting the section and checking.
    _check_stage_timeout() {
        local _stage="$1" _expected_s="$2"
        # Find the stage section and look for stage_timeout_s: N within it.
        # Use awk to extract from the stage heading to the next top-level entry.
        local _found
        _found="$(awk -v stage="$_stage:" '
            $0 == stage { in_stage=1; next }
            in_stage && /^[a-zA-Z_]/ { exit }
            in_stage && /stage_timeout_s:/ { print; exit }
        ' "$_simple" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[0-9]+')"

        if [[ "$_found" == "$_expected_s" ]]; then
            assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-6] simple.yaml $_stage: stage_timeout_s == ${_expected_s}s"
        else
            assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-6] simple.yaml $_stage: stage_timeout_s == ${_expected_s}s" \
                "got '${_found:-<absent>}'"
        fi
    }

    _check_stage_timeout "release" "30"
    _check_stage_timeout "persist" "120"
    _check_stage_timeout "test" "5400"
    _check_stage_timeout "build" "4200"
    _check_stage_timeout "design" "3900"
    _check_stage_timeout "plan" "1200"
    _check_stage_timeout "test-author" "900"
    _check_stage_timeout "spec-coverage" "600"
    _check_stage_timeout "acceptance-gate" "600"
    _check_stage_timeout "issue-acceptance" "600"
    _check_stage_timeout "spec-correspondence" "600"
    _check_stage_timeout "review_lenses" "600"
    _check_stage_timeout "intake" "600"
    _check_stage_timeout "pr" "600"
    _check_stage_timeout "hydrate" "600"
    _check_stage_timeout "secret-scan" "600"
    _check_stage_timeout "shape-floor" "600"
    _check_stage_timeout "design-gate" "600"
    _check_stage_timeout "gate-aggregator" "600"
    _check_stage_timeout "assertion-integrity" "600"
    _check_stage_timeout "review-aggregator" "600"

    # ─── [#1801/SPEC-6] release and persist have no router.timeout_s ──────────
    # The two always_run stages convert their router.timeout_s to stage_timeout_s.
    # After the change they must not declare router.timeout_s.
    for _ar_stage in release persist; do
        _router_to=""
        _router_to="$(awk -v stage="$_ar_stage:" '
            $0 == stage { in_stage=1; next }
            in_stage && /^[a-zA-Z_]/ { exit }
            in_stage && /router:/ { in_router=1; next }
            in_stage && in_router && /timeout_s:/ { print; exit }
            in_stage && in_router && /^[[:space:]]+[a-z_]+:/ && !/timeout_s/ { in_router=0 }
        ' "$_simple" 2>/dev/null || true)"

        if [[ -n "$_router_to" ]]; then
            assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-6] simple.yaml $_ar_stage: no router.timeout_s (converted to stage_timeout_s)" \
                "router.timeout_s still present: $_router_to"
        else
            assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-6] simple.yaml $_ar_stage: no router.timeout_s (converted to stage_timeout_s)"
        fi
    done
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-10] _runner_dispatch_always_run uses zbuild_pg_kill ──────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-10] _runner_dispatch_always_run uses zbuild_pg_kill"

if [[ -n "$_ar_body" ]]; then
    if grep -q 'zbuild_pg_kill' <<< "$_ar_body"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-10] _runner_dispatch_always_run calls zbuild_pg_kill"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] _runner_dispatch_always_run calls zbuild_pg_kill" \
            "zbuild_pg_kill not found in function body"
    fi

    # The hand-rolled `kill -TERM -- -` pattern must be gone from this function.
    # (The pattern is `kill -TERM -- -"$_ar_pid"` in the old code.)
    if grep -qE 'kill -TERM -- -"\$_ar_pid"' <<< "$_ar_body"; then
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] _runner_dispatch_always_run has no hand-rolled TERM/KILL sequence" \
            "found 'kill -TERM -- -\"\$_ar_pid\"' — replace with zbuild_pg_kill"
    else
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-10] _runner_dispatch_always_run has no hand-rolled TERM/KILL sequence"
    fi
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-10] lifecycle.sh uses zbuild_pg_kill for stage dispatch ──────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-10] lifecycle.sh uses zbuild_pg_kill (not hand-rolled TERM/KILL) for dispatch"

_lc="$REPO_ROOT/core/plugin-registry/lifecycle.sh"
if [[ ! -f "$_lc" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] core/plugin-registry/lifecycle.sh exists" "not found"
else
    if grep -q 'zbuild_pg_kill' "$_lc"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-10] lifecycle.sh calls zbuild_pg_kill for stage dispatch"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] lifecycle.sh calls zbuild_pg_kill for stage dispatch" \
            "zbuild_pg_kill not found — the per-dispatch watchdog must use it"
    fi
fi

cleanup_test_env
print_test_results
exit $((FAIL > 0))

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# [#1801/SPEC-8] Guard: orch-sequential is retired.
#
# After this change:
#   - plugins/tool/orch-sequential/ does not exist on disk
#   - no file outside docs/adr/ names "orch-sequential"
#   - configuring `sequential` as an orchestrator backend makes the run end as
#     `misconfigured`
#
# [#1801/SPEC-11] Guard: ADR-054 §9, ADR-017, and ADR-011 have ## Enforced by
# sections and are NOT in config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt.
#
# These tests FAIL on pre-change code (where orch-sequential still exists, where
# code files still reference it, and where the ADRs lack Enforced-by sections)
# and PASS after the change.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "[#1801/SPEC-8] orch-sequential retired; [#1801/SPEC-11] ADR Enforced-by sections"

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-8] the directory is absent ───────────────────────────────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-8] plugins/tool/orch-sequential/ is absent"

if [[ -e "$REPO_ROOT/plugins/tool/orch-sequential" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-8] plugins/tool/orch-sequential/ is absent" \
        "directory still exists — the retired backend was not removed"
else
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-8] plugins/tool/orch-sequential/ is absent"
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-8] no file outside docs/adr/ names orch-sequential ──────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-8] no file outside docs/adr/ names orch-sequential"

# Directories the guard allows: docs/adr/ (historical references are fine there)
# and tests/golden (the golden for the deleted plugin will also be gone).
# The guard runs via grep -r, excluding those two directories.
_bad_refs=""
while IFS= read -r _match; do
    [[ -z "$_match" ]] && continue
    # Strip repo root prefix for readability
    _rel="${_match#$REPO_ROOT/}"
    _bad_refs+="  $_rel"$'\n'
done < <(grep -rl 'orch-sequential' "$REPO_ROOT" \
    --exclude-dir='.git' \
    --exclude-dir='legacy-DoNotUse' 2>/dev/null | \
    grep -v '^'"$REPO_ROOT"'/docs/adr/' | \
    grep -v '^'"$REPO_ROOT"'/tests/golden/' | \
    grep -v '^'"$REPO_ROOT"'/tests/unit/orch-sequential-retired-guard-test\.sh$' || true)

if [[ -n "$_bad_refs" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-8] no file outside docs/adr/ names orch-sequential" \
        "found references:"$'\n'"$_bad_refs"
else
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-8] no file outside docs/adr/ names orch-sequential"
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-8] configuring sequential as backend → misconfigured ─────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-8] configuring sequential as a backend ends the run as misconfigured"

# source contract.sh with a controlled env so _orch_load_backend uses the
# sequential alias and we can capture its outcome.
_orch_result=""
_orch_rc=0
_orch_result="$(
    ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND=sequential \
    ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$REPO_ROOT/plugins" \
    bash -c '
        source "'"$REPO_ROOT"'/scripts/lib/helpers.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
        source "'"$REPO_ROOT"'/core/orch/contract.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
        # After the change, orch_load_backend emits orch.backend.misconfigured
        # or writes a misconfigured disposition; check what the function does.
        orch_load_backend sequential 2>&1
        echo "rc=$?"
    ' 2>&1)" || _orch_rc=$?

# The requirement: configuring sequential emits misconfigured
# Accept either an event name match or an explicit "misconfigured" in output
if grep -qiE 'misconfigured|sequential.*not found|backend.*sequential.*not' <<< "$_orch_result"; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-8] configuring sequential as backend signals misconfigured"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-8] configuring sequential as backend signals misconfigured" \
        "output: $(printf '%s' "$_orch_result" | head -5 | tr '\n' '|')"
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-054 has ## Enforced by section ──────────────────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-054 has ## Enforced by section"

_adr054="$REPO_ROOT/docs/adr/ADR-054-stage-contract.md"
if [[ ! -f "$_adr054" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-054 exists" "file not found: $_adr054"
else
    if grep -qE '^## Enforced by' "$_adr054"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-054 has ## Enforced by section"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-054 has ## Enforced by section" \
            "section absent — ADR-054 §9 requires it"
    fi
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-017 has ## Enforced by section ──────────────────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-017 has ## Enforced by section"

_adr017="$REPO_ROOT/docs/adr/ADR-017-per-stage-router-config.md"
if [[ ! -f "$_adr017" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-017 exists" "file not found: $_adr017"
else
    if grep -qE '^## Enforced by' "$_adr017"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-017 has ## Enforced by section"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-017 has ## Enforced by section" \
            "section absent"
    fi
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-011 has ## Enforced by section ──────────────────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-011 has ## Enforced by section"

_adr011="$REPO_ROOT/docs/adr/ADR-011-pluggable-backends.md"
if [[ ! -f "$_adr011" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-011 exists" "file not found: $_adr011"
else
    if grep -qE '^## Enforced by' "$_adr011"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-011 has ## Enforced by section"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-011 has ## Enforced by section" \
            "section absent"
    fi
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-11] the three ADRs are not in the enforcement baseline ───────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-054, ADR-017, ADR-011 removed from adr-enforcement-baseline.txt"

_baseline="$REPO_ROOT/config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt"
if [[ ! -f "$_baseline" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-11] config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt exists" \
        "file not found: $_baseline"
else
    for _adr_name in ADR-054 ADR-017 ADR-011; do
        if grep -q "$_adr_name" "$_baseline"; then
            assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-11] $_adr_name is not in adr-enforcement-baseline.txt" \
                "$_adr_name still listed — remove after adding its Enforced-by section"
        else
            assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-11] $_adr_name is not in adr-enforcement-baseline.txt"
        fi
    done
fi

print_test_results
exit $((FAIL > 0))

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
3	# ║  plugin-registry — lifecycle hook dispatch + fail-closed output scanner    ║
4	# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
5	#
6	# Split from registry.sh (#364). Owns the runtime dispatch path:
7	# `plugin_hook_call` (sources plugin.sh in an isolated subshell, applies
8	# pre-source tamper checks, calls the hook function, then verifies declared
9	# outputs) and `scan_plugin_outputs` (ADR-001 fail-closed artifact-presence
10	# scanner). Depends on yaml_get / verify_plugin_for_source from the other two
11	# split modules — sourced together via the registry.sh facade.
12	# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail settings; do not add set -euo pipefail.
13	
14	[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_REGISTRY_LIFECYCLE_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
15	_ZBUILD_REGISTRY_LIFECYCLE_LOADED=1
16	
17	# #1809 (ADR-058 C9): declared-output path resolution is shared with
18	# core/pipeline/write-boundary.sh so the artifact scanner and the write-boundary
19	# classifier can never disagree about where a declared output lives.
20	# shellcheck source=output-paths.sh
21	source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/output-paths.sh"
22	# shellcheck source=write-ownership.sh
23	source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/write-ownership.sh"
24	# shellcheck source=attempt-archive.sh
25	source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/attempt-archive.sh"
26	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/stage-dispatch-mark.sh
27	source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)/scripts/lib/stage-dispatch-mark.sh"
28	
29	# ─── scan_plugin_outputs — fail-closed artifact-presence scanner (#288) ─────
30	# ADR-001 §Fail-closed scanner contract:
31	#   "If a plugin declares an output but no artifact exists at outputs[].path
32	#    after run completes with exit 0, the engine emits a synthetic blocking
33	#    finding."
34	# #1906 retired provides.artifact_type, which the original wording keyed on;
35	# outputs[].required is the single declaration the scan now honours.
36	#
37	# Arguments:
38	#   $1 — plugin_dir
39	#   $2 — state_file (so $state_dir / $artifacts_dir can substitute into paths)
40	#
41	# Returns:
42	#   0 if all declared outputs are present (or no outputs declared).
43	#   1 if any declared output is missing — and emits one
44	#      `plugin.artifact.missing` event per missing path.
45	#
46	# Path-template substitution (Phase 0.5): supports ${state_dir} and
47	# ${artifact_dir} / ${artifacts_dir}. Any other ${VAR} resolves from the work
48	# unit's exported environment (#1803) — per-member outputs such as review-lens's
49	# `lens-${ZBUILD_REVIEW_LENS_ID}.json` (ADR-047 §2) are only checkable once the
50	# element var is expanded. A var that is unset stays literal and fails the check.
51	scan_plugin_outputs() {
52	    local plugin_dir="$1"
53	    local state_file="${2:-}"
54	    local stage="${3:-}"
55	    # #2252: `probe` answers present-or-not with no events, findings or marker.
56	    local probe="${4:-}"
57	    local manifest="$plugin_dir/manifest.yaml"
58	
59	    # No manifest, no outputs to scan — silently succeed.
60	    [[ ! -f "$manifest" ]] && return 0
61	
62	    local plugin_id; plugin_id="$(yaml_get "$manifest" "id" 2>/dev/null || true)"
63	    local kind; kind="$(yaml_get "$manifest" "kind" 2>/dev/null || true)"
64	    # ADR-047 §4 capability flag: build legitimately writes a zero-byte diff.patch
65	    # when a turn changed no code. The exemption is deliberately narrow — it never
66	    # covers a `primary: true` output, so a stage cannot mask an empty verdict
67	    # artifact (e.g. build-summary.json) by declaring the flag in its own manifest.
68	    local empty_diff_ok; empty_diff_ok="$(yaml_get "$manifest" "capabilities.empty_diff_legitimate" 2>/dev/null || true)"
69	
70	    # Compute substitution roots from state_file.
71	    local state_dir="" artifact_dir=""
72	    if [[ -n "$state_file" ]]; then
73	        state_dir="$(dirname "$state_file")"
74	        artifact_dir="${state_dir}/artifacts"
75	    fi
76	
77	    # Pull outputs[].path entries from the manifest. yaml_get/yaml_get_list
78	    # don't model lists of objects, so grep the YAML directly. Format we
79	    # support (per ADR-001):
80	    #   outputs:
81	    #     - name: foo
82	    #       path: ${artifact_dir}/foo.json
83	    #       type: foo.json
84	    # #511 F2: respect `required: false` on outputs. Without this, the scanner
85	    # would flag a legitimately optional artifact as a fail-closed contract
86	    # violation. (test_failures_summary was the original example; ADR-055 §9
87	    # since made it `required: true` — a summary is published on every terminal
88	    # verdict, so its absence IS a violation now.)
89	    local paths
90	    paths="$(_registry_output_path_rows "$manifest")"
91	
92	    [[ -z "$paths" ]] && return 0
93	
94	    local missing=0
95	    local raw_path raw_primary resolved _violation _event
96	    while IFS=$'\t' read -r raw_path raw_primary; do
97	        [[ -z "$raw_path" ]] && continue
98	        resolved="$(_registry_resolve_output_path "$raw_path" "$state_dir" "$artifact_dir")"
99	
100	        # An absent output always violates; a zero-byte one violates unless the
101	        # plugin declared the empty-diff capability AND this is not its primary.
102	        _violation=""
103	        if [[ ! -e "$resolved" ]]; then
104	            _violation="absent"
105	            _event="plugin.artifact.missing"
106	        elif [[ ! -s "$resolved" ]] &&
107	             ! { [[ "$empty_diff_ok" == "true" ]] && [[ "$raw_primary" != "true" ]]; }; then
108	            _violation="empty"
109	            _event="plugin.artifact.empty"
110	        fi
111	
112	        if [[ -n "$_violation" && "$probe" == "probe" ]]; then
113	            return 1
114	        fi
115	        if [[ -n "$_violation" ]]; then
116	            if [[ "$_violation" == "absent" ]]; then
117	                error "scan_plugin_outputs: plugin=$plugin_id declared output missing: $resolved (template: $raw_path)"
118	            else
119	                error "scan_plugin_outputs: plugin=$plugin_id declared output is empty (zero bytes): $resolved (template: $raw_path)"
120	            fi
121	            emit_event "$_event" \
122	                "plugin=$plugin_id" \
123	                "kind=$kind" \
124	                "expected_path=$resolved" \
125	                "template=$raw_path"
126	            # ADR-001 §Fail-closed contract: emit plugin.contract.violated and write
127	            # synthetic blocking findings.json so the output stage can surface the violation.
128	            local _stage_id="${stage:-${plugin_id}}"

548	        emit_event "plugin.$hook_name.complete" "plugin=$plugin_id" "kind=$kind"
549	    else
550	        emit_event "plugin.$hook_name.error" "plugin=$plugin_id" "kind=$kind" "rc=$rc"
551	    fi
552	
553	    # #2183: keep THIS attempt's declared outputs before the next dispatch can
554	    # overwrite them. After the rc branches, so a FAILED attempt — the one whose
555	    # record matters most — is archived too. Fail-open by construction.
556	    if [[ "$hook_name" == "run" ]] && declare -F attempt_archive_outputs >/dev/null 2>&1; then
557	        attempt_archive_outputs "$plugin_dir" "${2:-}" "${1:-}" "$rc" "$_lc_outputs_before" 2>/dev/null || true
558	    fi
559	
560	    # #1823 (ADR-054 §4): the plugin's raw status passes through UNCHANGED, and
561	    # deliberately so during versioned coexistence. A v1 plugin has no result
562	    # field in which to say what its rc says — `plan`'s rc=10 IS its only way to
563	    # report `scope_too_large` — so narrowing here would destroy the meaning of
564	    # every unmigrated plugin at once. The narrowing is gated on the result
565	    # contract at the dispatch boundary instead (see cycle_dispatch_stage), and
566	    # becomes unconditional in #1850 when the last v1 reader is dropped.
567	    return $rc
568	}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  plugin-registry — lifecycle hook dispatch + fail-closed output scanner    ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Split from registry.sh (#364). Owns the runtime dispatch path:
# `plugin_hook_call` (sources plugin.sh in an isolated subshell, applies
# pre-source tamper checks, calls the hook function, then verifies declared
# outputs) and `scan_plugin_outputs` (ADR-001 fail-closed artifact-presence
# scanner). Depends on yaml_get / verify_plugin_for_source from the other two
# split modules — sourced together via the registry.sh facade.
# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail settings; do not add set -euo pipefail.

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_REGISTRY_LIFECYCLE_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_REGISTRY_LIFECYCLE_LOADED=1

# #1809 (ADR-058 C9): declared-output path resolution is shared with
# core/pipeline/write-boundary.sh so the artifact scanner and the write-boundary
# classifier can never disagree about where a declared output lives.
# shellcheck source=output-paths.sh
source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/output-paths.sh"
# shellcheck source=write-ownership.sh
source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/write-ownership.sh"
# shellcheck source=attempt-archive.sh
source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/attempt-archive.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/stage-dispatch-mark.sh
source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)/scripts/lib/stage-dispatch-mark.sh"

# ─── scan_plugin_outputs — fail-closed artifact-presence scanner (#288) ─────
# ADR-001 §Fail-closed scanner contract:
#   "If a plugin declares an output but no artifact exists at outputs[].path
#    after run completes with exit 0, the engine emits a synthetic blocking
#    finding."
# #1906 retired provides.artifact_type, which the original wording keyed on;
# outputs[].required is the single declaration the scan now honours.
#
# Arguments:
#   $1 — plugin_dir
#   $2 — state_file (so $state_dir / $artifacts_dir can substitute into paths)
#
# Returns:
#   0 if all declared outputs are present (or no outputs declared).
#   1 if any declared output is missing — and emits one
#      `plugin.artifact.missing` event per missing path.
#
# Path-template substitution (Phase 0.5): supports ${state_dir} and
# ${artifact_dir} / ${artifacts_dir}. Any other ${VAR} resolves from the work
# unit's exported environment (#1803) — per-member outputs such as review-lens's
# `lens-${ZBUILD_REVIEW_LENS_ID}.json` (ADR-047 §2) are only checkable once the
# element var is expanded. A var that is unset stays literal and fails the check.
scan_plugin_outputs() {
    local plugin_dir="$1"
    local state_file="${2:-}"
    local stage="${3:-}"
    # #2252: `probe` answers present-or-not with no events, findings or marker.
    local probe="${4:-}"
    local manifest="$plugin_dir/manifest.yaml"

    # No manifest, no outputs to scan — silently succeed.
    [[ ! -f "$manifest" ]] && return 0

    local plugin_id; plugin_id="$(yaml_get "$manifest" "id" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    local kind; kind="$(yaml_get "$manifest" "kind" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    # ADR-047 §4 capability flag: build legitimately writes a zero-byte diff.patch
    # when a turn changed no code. The exemption is deliberately narrow — it never
    # covers a `primary: true` output, so a stage cannot mask an empty verdict
    # artifact (e.g. build-summary.json) by declaring the flag in its own manifest.
    local empty_diff_ok; empty_diff_ok="$(yaml_get "$manifest" "capabilities.empty_diff_legitimate" 2>/dev/null || true)"

    # Compute substitution roots from state_file.
    local state_dir="" artifact_dir=""
    if [[ -n "$state_file" ]]; then
        state_dir="$(dirname "$state_file")"
        artifact_dir="${state_dir}/artifacts"
    fi

    # Pull outputs[].path entries from the manifest. yaml_get/yaml_get_list
    # don't model lists of objects, so grep the YAML directly. Format we
    # support (per ADR-001):
    #   outputs:
    #     - name: foo
    #       path: ${artifact_dir}/foo.json
    #       type: foo.json
    # #511 F2: respect `required: false` on outputs. Without this, the scanner
    # would flag a legitimately optional artifact as a fail-closed contract
    # violation. (test_failures_summary was the original example; ADR-055 §9
    # since made it `required: true` — a summary is published on every terminal
    # verdict, so its absence IS a violation now.)
    local paths
    paths="$(_registry_output_path_rows "$manifest")"

    [[ -z "$paths" ]] && return 0

    local missing=0
    local raw_path raw_primary resolved _violation _event
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r raw_path raw_primary; do
        [[ -z "$raw_path" ]] && continue
        resolved="$(_registry_resolve_output_path "$raw_path" "$state_dir" "$artifact_dir")"

        # An absent output always violates; a zero-byte one violates unless the
        # plugin declared the empty-diff capability AND this is not its primary.
        _violation=""
        if [[ ! -e "$resolved" ]]; then
            _violation="absent"
            _event="plugin.artifact.missing"
        elif [[ ! -s "$resolved" ]] &&
             ! { [[ "$empty_diff_ok" == "true" ]] && [[ "$raw_primary" != "true" ]]; }; then
            _violation="empty"
            _event="plugin.artifact.empty"
        fi

        if [[ -n "$_violation" && "$probe" == "probe" ]]; then
            return 1
        fi
        if [[ -n "$_violation" ]]; then
            if [[ "$_violation" == "absent" ]]; then
                error "scan_plugin_outputs: plugin=$plugin_id declared output missing: $resolved (template: $raw_path)"
            else
                error "scan_plugin_outputs: plugin=$plugin_id declared output is empty (zero bytes): $resolved (template: $raw_path)"
            fi
            emit_event "$_event" \
                "plugin=$plugin_id" \
                "kind=$kind" \
                "expected_path=$resolved" \
                "template=$raw_path"
            # ADR-001 §Fail-closed contract: emit plugin.contract.violated and write
            # synthetic blocking findings.json so the output stage can surface the violation.
            local _stage_id="${stage:-${plugin_id}}"
            emit_event "plugin.contract.violated" \
                "stage=$_stage_id" \
                "plugin=$plugin_id" \
                "expected_path=$resolved" \
                "reason=artifact_missing_or_empty"
            if [[ -n "$state_dir" ]]; then
                mkdir -p "${state_dir}/artifacts"
                local _findings_file="${state_dir}/artifacts/${_stage_id}-${plugin_id}-contract-violated-findings.json"
                jq -n \
                    --arg stage "$_stage_id" \
                    --arg plugin "$plugin_id" \
                    --arg path "$resolved" \
                    --arg violation "$_violation" \
                    '{
                        schema_version: 1,
                        findings: [{
                            id: "artifact-contract-violated",
                            title: ("Plugin contract violated: " + $plugin +
                                    (if $violation == "empty"
                                     then " wrote an empty (zero-byte) required output"
                                     else " declared a required output but wrote no artifact" end)),
                            severity: "blocking",
                            stage: $stage,
                            plugin: $plugin,
                            detail: ("Expected artifact at: " + $path)
                        }]
                    }' > "$_findings_file" 2>/dev/null || true
                # #1809: file-backed marker so runner_read_stage_disposition (a separate
                # process under map:) can detect the violation and return broken.
                mkdir -p "${state_dir}/runtime"
                touch "${state_dir}/runtime/artifact-contract-violated" 2>/dev/null || true
            fi
            missing=$((missing + 1))
        fi
    done <<< "$paths"

    return $((missing > 0))
}

# ─── _lc_owned_by_others_deny <state_dir> <stage> (#2189) ────────────────────
# One absolute path per line: every file a stage OTHER than <stage> reported
# owning (artifacts/stage-reports.json). Empty when nothing is owned.
_lc_owned_by_others_deny() {
    local rec="${1:-}/artifacts/stage-reports.json" me="${2:-}"
    [[ -s "$rec" ]] || return 0
    # Read without a fork: nothing owned (most runs) needs no jq at all.
    local _body; _body="$(<"$rec")"
    [[ "$_body" == *'"owned_files"'* ]] || return 0
    jq -r --arg me "$me" --arg root "${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-.}" '
        [(.owned_files // {}) | to_entries[] | select(.key != $me) | .value[] | "\($root)/\(.)"]
        | unique[]' <<< "$_body" 2>/dev/null
}

# ─── plugin_hook_call ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Source the plugin's plugin.sh and call a lifecycle hook by name.
# Plugin functions are isolated by sub-shell to prevent namespace pollution.
plugin_hook_call() {
    local plugin_dir="$1"
    local hook_name="$2"   # run | cleanup (or kind-specific)
    shift 2
    local manifest="$plugin_dir/manifest.yaml"
    local plugin_sh="$plugin_dir/plugin.sh"

    # ADR-068 §8: mark when this run of the stage started, FIRST — before any
    # refusal below can return — so a run that writes no result, refused or
    # not, is never credited with the previous run's (stage_result_is_current).
    [[ "$hook_name" == "run" ]] && stage_dispatch_mark "${2:-}" "${1:-}"

    if [[ ! -f "$plugin_sh" ]]; then
        error "plugin_hook_call: plugin.sh missing: $plugin_sh"
        return 1
    fi

    local plugin_id; plugin_id="$(yaml_get "$manifest" "id")"
    local kind; kind="$(yaml_get "$manifest" "kind")"

    # ADR-054 §3 (#1862): the engine states, for exactly the span of one
    # dispatch, which stage this is and which plugin serves it.
    #
    # A plugin IS self-defining about what it is — plugin-bootstrap.sh resolves
    # _ZBUILD_PLUGIN_DIR from its own BASH_SOURCE, and 18 plugins do. It can
    # never be self-defining about which STAGE it is: `review_lenses`
    # (simple.yaml) is served by plugin `review-lens` via role `review_lens` —
    # three namespaces the template alone maps, and under `map:` all six lens
    # members receive that one stage name. Everything keyed to the flow (the
    # timeline, stage_statuses, the per-stage router knobs) needs the stage
    # name; introspection can only ever yield the plugin id.
    #
    # `local -x`, not `export`, for three reasons: it reaches the emit_event
    # calls below, which fire OUTSIDE the plugin subshell (the blank envelope
    # .plugin/.kind of #1705); it reaches the subshell and anything it spawns;
    # and it unsets on return, so stage N's identity cannot bleed into stage
    # N+1 — a plain export would trade a blank field for a stale one.
    #
    # This is the only site that reaches all four dispatch arms. The `map:` arm
    # runs a generated standalone script (strategies/common.sh) the runner
    # cannot export into — but plugin_hook_call is its last line.
    #
    # ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT is deliberately NOT set: it is an operator override
    # every reader spells `${ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT:-<default>}`, and ADR-024 /
    # persona-resolve.sh forbid relying on it as a root. Derive from
    # ZBUILD_PLUGIN_DIR instead.
    #
    # Stage id is $1 post-shift for both hooks — run(stage_id, state_file, ...)
    # and cleanup(stage_id, state_file, scope), ADR-054 §2. Same assumption
    # scan_plugin_outputs already makes below.
    #
    # `:-` is deliberate and deliberately unlike `stage_arg="${1:-}"` below: an
    # empty $1 keeps the ambient stage rather than blanking it. A caller with no
    # stage to name must not erase the one its own caller established — the
    # throttle marker's path is keyed on this value and is written inside the
    # dispatch but read outside it (router-rc-classify.sh:154), so a blank here
    # would split the key across the boundary. scan_plugin_outputs has no such
    # cross-boundary reader and wants the literal argument.
    local -x ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE="${1:-${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}}"
    # #1706 (ADR-054 §3.1): the unit's own name — the stage, or <stage>.<element>
    # for a map member — for this dispatch only. The element is consumed here, so
    # a stage dispatched from inside the member is named by its own stage.
    local -x ZBUILD_UNIT="${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE}${ZBUILD_UNIT_ELEMENT:+.${ZBUILD_UNIT_ELEMENT}}"
    local -x ZBUILD_UNIT_ELEMENT=""
    local -x ZBUILD_PLUGIN="$plugin_id"
    local -x ZBUILD_PLUGIN_KIND="$kind"
    local -x ZBUILD_PLUGIN_DIR="$plugin_dir"

    # ADR-058 §2 (#1918): the engine states WHERE this stage may write, for
    # exactly the span of one dispatch. #1809 makes a declared output a write
    # boundary; a boundary cannot be enforced until the permitted areas are
    # defined, and the per-stage scratch area did not exist at all.
    #
    # Same site and same `local -x` as the identity block above, for the same
    # reasons: it is the only site reaching all four dispatch arms (the `map:`
    # arm runs a generated standalone script the runner cannot export into, and
    # this call is that script's last line), and `local -x` restores the prior
    # value AND the prior export attribute on return, so stage N's scratch
    # cannot bleed into stage N+1 and the test harness's sandboxed
    # ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR (scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh) comes back intact.
    #
    # Guarded on `$2` being an ABSOLUTE path — the state_file, post-shift, per
    # ADR-054 §2, the same argument scan_plugin_outputs reads below.
    #
    # Absolute, not merely non-empty, and the difference is load-bearing.
    # `dirname` of a bare relative name is `.`, and by the time a stage
    # dispatches, the runner has cd'd into the RUN'S WORKTREE (ADR-052) — so a
    # relative state_file would put `scratch/` and `artifacts/` inside the
    # repository under change. That is the exact leak this block exists to close,
    # reintroduced by the block itself.
    #
    # It cannot happen from the engine: runner.sh absolutizes state_dir "BEFORE
    # anything derives a path from state_dir" precisely so no caller has to think
    # about this (ADR-052, #1640). A relative or empty `$2` therefore means an
    # ad-hoc caller — the `plugin_hook_call … ""` of
    # tests/unit/plugin-lifecycle-event-balance-test.sh, or the positional
    # `… "arg1" "arg2"` of tests/integration/core-plugin-registry-test.sh — which
    # has no job folder to be inside and must reach the plugin with the
    # environment it has today.
    #
    # Setting TMPDIR is the load-bearing part. scripts/lib/env-scrub.sh
    # wildcard-unsets every ZBUILD_* before each model spawn — with the
    # unset-until-gone loop #1873 added specifically to defeat `local -x`
    # layering at this seam — while TMPDIR is explicitly PRESERVED. It is
    # therefore the only channel that reaches the model. Redirecting it puts the
    # model's own temp writes in bounds and relocates every `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}`
    # consumer in the engine and the plugins with zero plugin edits.
    #
    # ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR is a definition, not a leak fix: the gate plugins test
    # for a live state file first and only fall back to temp when invoked
    # ad-hoc, so their outputs land correctly today. What changes is that the
    # plugin's own fallback and scan_plugin_outputs' `${artifact_dir}`
    # substitution below become the same directory BY CONSTRUCTION, instead of
    # two independent derivations that a caller can silently split.
    if [[ "${2:-}" == /* ]]; then
        local _ws_state_dir; _ws_state_dir="$(dirname "$2")"
        local -x ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR="${_ws_state_dir}/artifacts"

        # #2022: the acceptance TESTFILES belong to the stage that AUTHORS them.
        # Every other spawn is denied Edit() on them, so build cannot rewrite an
        # assertion to agree with its own implementation. Derived from the role
        # the plugin declares, never from a stage id: naming `build` here would
        # be a stage naming a stage, the shape #1767 removed from routing.
        # core/router/permissions.sh renders the rules; the decision is here.
        local -x ZBUILD_PERMISSION_DENY_EDIT=""
        # #2170: `$1` here is the STAGE ID — the function `shift 2`s its
        # plugin_dir/hook_name arguments away above. Looked up on the stage id
        # the role was always empty, so the author was denied its own testfiles
        # (invisible while the rule rendered as `Edit(/abs)`, #2163).
        # #2189: files ANOTHER stage reported owning (test-author reports the
        # testfiles it authored) — from the run's stage-reports record, never
        # design.md by path and never a role name. The owner is not denied.
        ZBUILD_PERMISSION_DENY_EDIT+="$(_lc_owned_by_others_deny "$_ws_state_dir" "${1:-}")"
        [[ -n "$ZBUILD_PERMISSION_DENY_EDIT" ]] && ZBUILD_PERMISSION_DENY_EDIT+=$'\n'

        # #2174: write ownership from the manifests (write-ownership.sh) —
        # other plugins' declared outputs, and the repo unless declared.
        _lc_other_outputs_deny "$plugin_dir" "$_ws_state_dir"   # parent shell: fills the memo
        ZBUILD_PERMISSION_DENY_EDIT+="$_LC_DENY_OUT"
        local _lc_wr; _lc_wr="$(manifest_index_get "$manifest" capabilities.writes_repository 2>/dev/null)" \
            || _lc_wr="$(yaml_get "$manifest" "capabilities.writes_repository" 2>/dev/null || true)"
        if [[ "${_lc_wr%$'\n'}" != "true" ]]; then
            _lc_repo_entries_deny "${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-.}"
            ZBUILD_PERMISSION_DENY_EDIT+="$_LC_DENY_OUT"
        fi

        if ! declare -F stage_scratch_ensure >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            # shellcheck source=../pipeline/stage-scratch.sh
            source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../pipeline" && pwd)/stage-scratch.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
        fi
        if declare -F stage_scratch_ensure >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            local _ws_scratch
            # Fail-open: an unnameable stage or an uncreatable directory leaves
            # both vars unset and every consumer on the fallback it has today.
            # A stage must not be refused dispatch because scratch was
            # unavailable — that would make a diagnostic convenience a new way
            # for a run to die.
            if _ws_scratch="$(stage_scratch_ensure "$_ws_state_dir" "${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}" "${ZBUILD_MAP_ELEMENT:-}" 2>/dev/null)" \
               && [[ -n "$_ws_scratch" ]]; then
                local -x ZBUILD_STAGE_SCRATCH="$_ws_scratch"
                local -x TMPDIR="$_ws_scratch"
            fi
        fi

        # #2024: this seam records that a stage STARTED. It does not record a
        # process group, and the distinction is the whole point.
        #
        # It used to write `<stage>.pgid` from `$$`, which conflated two jobs.
        # As a process handle it was inert: a stage is a bash function call, so
        # no group exists at this seam and `$$` names the ENGINE's group, which
        # teardown then skipped — correctly, since signalling your own group
        # takes the runner down. But as a STARTED MARKER it was load-bearing:
        # `stage_statuses` is written only when a stage completes, so a stage
        # killed mid-flight is known to teardown by this file alone.
        #
        # One file could not honestly be both. Groups are registered by whoever
        # creates one (zbuild_pg_register); this writes `<stage>.started`, and
        # nothing reads it as a pgid. Do not reinstate a `.pgid` write here: any
        # pgid observable at dispatch cannot be signalled from inside the run.
        if [[ "$hook_name" == "run" && -n "${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}" ]]; then
            local _st_dir="${_ws_state_dir}/runtime/stages"
            if mkdir -p "$_st_dir" 2>/dev/null; then
                # One path component, so no stage name can climb out of runtime/.
                local _st_key="${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE//[^A-Za-z0-9_-]/_}"
                # Fail-open: a stage is never refused dispatch over bookkeeping.
                : > "${_st_dir}/${_st_key}.started" 2>/dev/null || true
            fi
        fi

        # #1809 (ADR-058 C9): load the write-boundary enforcer lazily, same
        # pattern as stage-scratch.sh above. Fail-open: an unloadable module
        # leaves the mark unset and write_boundary_check returns 0 immediately.
        if ! declare -F write_boundary_mark >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            # shellcheck source=../pipeline/write-boundary.sh
            source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../pipeline" && pwd)/write-boundary.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
        fi
    fi

    # ADR-055 §1 (#1826): the engine resolves what this stage DECLARED it needs
    # and states where each artifact is, so a plugin stops hardcoding filenames.
    # Same site and same `local -x` as the identity vars above, for the same two
    # reasons: it is the only site reaching all four dispatch arms (the `map:` arm
    # runs a generated standalone script the runner cannot export into, and this
    # call is that script's last line), and `local -x` unsets on return so stage
    # N's index cannot bleed into stage N+1.
    #
    # Unconditional as of #1825 — the resolved-input index is always built and
    # never declared, so the dispatch is byte-identical to today.
    #
    # plugins_root is derived from plugin_dir (plugins/<kind>/<id>/), not read
    # from ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT — ADR-024 / persona-resolve.sh forbid relying on
    # that override as a root, exactly as the block above says.
    if [[ "$hook_name" == "run" ]]; then
        if ! declare -F _inputs_resolve_stage >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            # shellcheck source=../pipeline/input-resolve.sh
            source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../pipeline" && pwd)/input-resolve.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
        fi
        if declare -F _inputs_resolve_stage >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            local _ir_proot; _ir_proot="$(cd "$plugin_dir/../.." 2>/dev/null && pwd)"
            local _ir_state="${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-}"
            if [[ -n "$_ir_state" && -n "$ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE" ]]; then
                # Pre-dispatch: a missing `required: true` input means the stage
                # is never launched — we return before plugin.sh is sourced, so
                # its entrypoint does not run at all.
                #
                # rc=1, not a private code: ADR-054 §4 narrows this boundary to
                # {0,1} and dispatch-rc-guard-test.sh ratchets it. "Which input,
                # from which producer" rides the refusal render and the
                # plugin.run.refused event — the declared channels — exactly as
                # the lockfile-mismatch refusal below does.
                if ! _inputs_check_required "$ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE" "$_ir_proot" "$_ir_state" "$manifest"; then
                    emit_event "plugin.$hook_name.refused" "plugin=$plugin_id" "kind=$kind" \
                        "reason=required-input-missing"
                    return 1
                fi
                local -x ZBUILD_STAGE_INPUTS
                ZBUILD_STAGE_INPUTS="$(_inputs_resolve_stage "$ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE" "$_ir_proot" "$_ir_state" "$manifest" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            fi
        fi
    fi

    local hook_fn; hook_fn="$(yaml_get "$manifest" "hooks.$hook_name")"
    if [[ -z "$hook_fn" ]]; then
        if [[ "$hook_name" == "cleanup" ]]; then
            # #1823 (ADR-054 §4): an absent OPTIONAL hook had nothing to do and
            # did it — rc 0. The absence is not lost: it rides
            # `plugin.cleanup.absent`, a declared channel, which is what #1828's
            # own acceptance asked for ("distinguishable in the engine's
            # RECORDS"). ADR-056 additionally returned rc=3 for this, justified
            # against ADR-001's "0=ok, 1=recoverable, 2=fatal" — the very table
            # ADR-054 §4 supersedes. Nothing in the engine ever read it.
            #
            # Consumers that need to tell "skipped" from "ran cleanly" — #1829's
            # teardown dispatch and #1830's teardown stage — read the event.
            # Two channels carrying one fact is the defect this contract exists
            # to end, and the rc is the one that cannot be enforced.
            emit_event "plugin.$hook_name.absent" "plugin=$plugin_id" "kind=$kind"
            return 0
        fi
        # Absent required hook: emit refused event and fail.
        emit_event "plugin.$hook_name.refused" "plugin=$plugin_id" "kind=$kind" "reason=hook-not-declared"
        return 1
    fi

    # Pre-source tamper check (#290). Honors ZBUILD_STRICT_PLUGIN_LOCK.
    if ! verify_plugin_for_source "$manifest"; then
        emit_event "plugin.$hook_name.refused" "plugin=$plugin_id" "kind=$kind" "reason=lockfile-mismatch"
        return 1
    fi

    # #1809 (ADR-058 C9): mark the dispatch start so write_boundary_check can
    # find files written during this dispatch. Fail-open: missing function = no-op.
    if declare -F write_boundary_mark >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        # Keyed on stage + map element so nested, map and parallel dispatches
        # against one state file do not share (and re-stamp) one window.
        write_boundary_mark "${2:-}" "${1:-}" "${ZBUILD_MAP_ELEMENT:-}" || true
    fi

    # #2186: what the declared outputs were before this run, so the attempt
    # record can say which ones the run actually changed. Fail-open.
    local _lc_outputs_before=""
    if [[ "$hook_name" == "run" ]] && declare -F attempt_outputs_fingerprint >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        _lc_outputs_before="$(attempt_outputs_fingerprint "$plugin_dir" "${2:-}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    fi

    emit_event "plugin.$hook_name.start" "plugin=$plugin_id" "kind=$kind"

    # Run in a subshell to isolate plugin's variables/functions
    (
        # shellcheck disable=SC1090
        source "$plugin_sh"
        if declare -F "$hook_fn" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            "$hook_fn" "$@"
        else
            echo "plugin_hook_call: function $hook_fn not defined in $plugin_sh" >&2
            exit 1
        fi
    )
    local rc=$?

    if [[ $rc -eq 0 ]]; then
        # #288: after a successful `run`, verify the plugin actually produced
        # the artifacts it declared. Absent evidence IS blocking evidence —
        # emit synthetic findings for each missing output and surface the
        # failure as a non-zero hook exit so the caller can react.
        if [[ "$hook_name" == "run" ]]; then
            # Per ADR-001 hook signature: $@ after shift 2 is (stage_id, state_file, ...).
            local stage_arg="${1:-}"
            local state_file_arg="${2:-}"
            # #2252: a stage that SAYS it did not finish (timed_out, out_of_turns,
            # interrupted) is expected to be missing outputs — failing it for them
            # overwrote its retryable word with `broken` and halted the run
            # (#1844: design timed out, and the run ended instead of retrying).
            # Its own word stands; the retry rule decides what happens next.
            # Read the stage's word only when an output IS missing (a quiet
            # probe first): the read costs several jq calls per dispatch, and a
            # probe that passes means there is nothing for the full check to say.
            local _lcr_state="" _lcr_contract="" _lcr_verdict="" _lcr_disp="" _lcr_reason="" \
                  _lcr_viol="" _lcr_path="" _lcr_present="" _lc_unfinished="" _lc_missing=0
            scan_plugin_outputs "$plugin_dir" "$state_file_arg" "$stage_arg" probe 2>/dev/null || _lc_missing=1
            if (( _lc_missing )) && declare -F _verdict_read_result >/dev/null 2>&1 \
                    && declare -F disposition_unfinished >/dev/null 2>&1 \
                    && [[ -n "$state_file_arg" ]]; then
                _verdict_read_result "$(dirname "$state_file_arg")" "$manifest" "$stage_arg" 0 _lcr 2>/dev/null || true
                disposition_unfinished "${_lcr_disp:-}" && _lc_unfinished="$_lcr_disp"
            fi
            if [[ -n "$_lc_unfinished" ]]; then
                emit_event "plugin.$hook_name.artifact_check_skipped" "plugin=$plugin_id" \
                    "kind=$kind" "disposition=$_lc_unfinished"
            elif (( _lc_missing )) && ! scan_plugin_outputs "$plugin_dir" "$state_file_arg" "$stage_arg"; then
                emit_event "plugin.$hook_name.artifact_check_failed" \
                    "plugin=$plugin_id" "kind=$kind"
                # A dispatch that STARTED must also END. This arm and the
                # write-boundary arm below both `return 1` from inside the rc=0
                # branch, so neither reaches the `complete` emit nor the `else`
                # arm's `error` emit — the start was left without a partner and
                # the run's own log could not say which stage died (run
                # 33899683569: 54 start, 48 complete, 5 error). `reason=` is a
                # data field on an already-declared event name, so the event-NAME
                # set is unchanged and the sequence goldens are untouched.
                emit_event "plugin.$hook_name.error" "plugin=$plugin_id" \
                    "kind=$kind" "rc=1" "reason=artifact-check-failed"
                return 1
            fi
            # #1809 (ADR-058 C9): sweep for writes outside declared outputs and
            # engine-owned areas. Fail-open: unloaded module = write_boundary_check
            # undefined = this arm is unreachable.
            if declare -F write_boundary_check >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                _ZBUILD_WB_ACTION=""
                if ! write_boundary_check "$plugin_dir" "$state_file_arg" "$stage_arg" \
                        "${ZBUILD_MAP_ELEMENT:-}"; then
                    # See the artifact-check arm above: same missing-terminal
                    # defect. write_boundary_violation_recorded has already named
                    # the offending path on its own three channels; this event
                    # is what closes the start/end pair.
                    local _wb_reason="write-boundary-violation"
                    [[ "${_ZBUILD_WB_ACTION:-}" == "reverted" ]] && _wb_reason="write-boundary-reverted"
                    emit_event "plugin.$hook_name.error" "plugin=$plugin_id" \
                        "kind=$kind" "rc=1" "reason=$_wb_reason"
                    return 1
                fi
            fi
        fi
        emit_event "plugin.$hook_name.complete" "plugin=$plugin_id" "kind=$kind"
    else
        emit_event "plugin.$hook_name.error" "plugin=$plugin_id" "kind=$kind" "rc=$rc"
    fi

    # #2183: keep THIS attempt's declared outputs before the next dispatch can
    # overwrite them. After the rc branches, so a FAILED attempt — the one whose
    # record matters most — is archived too. Fail-open by construction.
    if [[ "$hook_name" == "run" ]] && declare -F attempt_archive_outputs >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        attempt_archive_outputs "$plugin_dir" "${2:-}" "${1:-}" "$rc" "$_lc_outputs_before" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi

    # #1823 (ADR-054 §4): the plugin's raw status passes through UNCHANGED, and
    # deliberately so during versioned coexistence. A v1 plugin has no result
    # field in which to say what its rc says — `plan`'s rc=10 IS its only way to
    # report `scope_too_large` — so narrowing here would destroy the meaning of
    # every unmigrated plugin at once. The narrowing is gated on the result
    # contract at the dispatch boundary instead (see cycle_dispatch_stage), and
    # becomes unconditional in #1850 when the last v1 reader is dropped.
    return $rc
}

112	_usage() {

116	                 [--resume] [--from-stage <stage>] [--no-resume] [--force]
117	  --issue <N>       GitHub issue number to work
118	  --goal "<text>"   Pipeline goal description (alternative to --issue)
119	  --dry-run         Print the stage plan without executing anything
120	  --template <id>   Pipeline template to use (default: simple)
121	  --resume          Resume an existing run (skip completed stages)
122	  --from-stage <s>  Skip ahead to stage <s> when resuming (emits warning)
123	  --no-resume       Recreate: start fresh even if a state exists and restore no
124	                    prior-run work (default: resume, reusing prior work;
125	                    ZBUILD_RESUME=0 is the same, #2225)
126	  --force           Resume even if status=aborted
127	  --self-host       Dogfood zBuild's own engine: redirect read-only contract-
128	                    grammar libs to a working-tree snapshot (#963, ADR-023)

132	  ZBUILD_SCOPE_PATHS        Newline-delimited scope paths; written as '+ <path>' entries.
133	  ZBUILD_SELF_HOST          Set to 1 to enable self-host mode (same as --self-host).

146	_runner_run_id="" _runner_issue="" _runner_ended=false _runner_state_file=""

148	# reported once rather than once per stage boundary.

151	# ─── _runner_retry_budget <stage> (#2187, was #1887's redispatch budget) ─────
152	# How many times a stage whose disposition says `retry` is re-dispatched. The
153	# word never carries a count: the template's per-stage `retry:` wins, then the
154	# ZBUILD_DISPOSITION_REDISPATCH knob, then the engine default 3. Capped at 5 —
155	# the cycle re-runs its members anyway, so this is not a budget for grinding.
156	# A value above the cap clamps to the cap; a non-number is ignored.
157	_runner_retry_budget() {
158	    local v=""
159	    if declare -F template_stage_retry >/dev/null 2>&1; then
160	        v="$(template_stage_retry "${1:-}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
161	    fi
162	    [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || v="${ZBUILD_DISPOSITION_REDISPATCH:-}"
163	    [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || v=3
164	    (( v > 5 )) && v=5
165	    printf '%s' "$v"
166	}

168	# ─── _runner_leaf_contract_halt <state_file> <stage> <reason> ───────────────
169	# A leaf stage whose v2 result the engine rejected ends the run; rc 0 when it
170	# did. A cycle already halts on this (#550); a leaf recorded `error` and went on,
171	# which is how #1835's run shipped a plan result with no `reason`. Safe ahead of
172	# #1798: a contract violation is a zBuild defect (ADR-054 §6 `broken`), never a
173	# transient failure, so this cannot turn a network hiccup into a dead run.
174	# Reads main()'s _runner_run_id / _runner_issue and sets its _runner_ended.
175	_runner_leaf_contract_halt() {
176	    local sf="$1" st="$2" why="${3:-}"
177	    [[ "$why" == contract_violation:* ]] || return 1
178	    _update_stage_status "$sf" "$st" "failed"
179	    _set_pipeline_status "$sf" "failed"
180	    eb_emit_event "stage.fail" "stage=$st" "reason=$why" 2>/dev/null || true
181	    eb_emit_event "pipeline.end" "status=failed" "stage=$st" "reason=$why" \
182	        "run_id=${_runner_run_id:-}" "issue=${_runner_issue:-}" 2>/dev/null || true
183	    _render_pipeline_end "failed" "$st"
184	    _runner_ended=true
185	    error "Stage $st wrote a result the engine rejects ($why) — a zBuild defect; the run stops here"
186	    return 0

189	# ─── _runner_leaf_verdict_halt <state_file> <stage> <class> <raw> ────────────
190	# #1798 (ADR-054 §4): a leaf stage that reports a failure ends the run; rc 0
191	# when it did. <class> is the classified verdict the runner already read
192	# (runner_read_stage_verdict: fail, or a structural word passed through);
193	# <raw> is the stage's own word, which the run's end names. A cycle acts on its
194	# members' verdicts; a leaf used to record one, pick a glyph from it and
195	# complete anyway. A template opts a stage out with `blocking: false`
196	# (ADR-013) — advisory by declaration, never by accident.
197	_runner_leaf_verdict_halt() {
198	    local sf="$1" st="$2" v="${3:-}" raw="${4:-}"
199	    case "$v" in
200	        fail|error|block|scope_violation|corrupt_diff) ;;
201	        *) return 1 ;;
202	    esac
203	    [[ "$(template_stage_blocking "$st" 2>/dev/null)" == "false" ]] && return 1
204	    [[ -n "$raw" && "$raw" != "missing" ]] || raw="$v"
205	    _update_stage_status "$sf" "$st" "failed"
206	    _zbuild_state_set_stage_verdict "$sf" "$st" "$v"
207	    _set_pipeline_status "$sf" "failed"
208	    # No `rc=` field: the stage exited 0, so a verdict-triggered stage.fail
209	    # carries the stage's word (`verdict=`) instead — as the contract halt
210	    # carries `reason=` alone. A consumer of stage.fail reads either shape.
211	    eb_emit_event "stage.fail" "stage=$st" "verdict=$raw" "reason=stage_failed:$raw" 2>/dev/null || true
212	    eb_emit_event "pipeline.end" "status=failed" "stage=$st" "reason=stage_failed:$raw" \
213	        "run_id=${_runner_run_id:-}" "issue=${_runner_issue:-}" 2>/dev/null || true
214	    _render_pipeline_end "failed" "$st"
215	    _runner_ended=true
216	    error "Stage $st reported $raw — the run stops here"
217	    return 0
218	}
